newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish fin min says EMU timetable still holds.
newsitem.headline: Swedish fin min says EMU timetable still holds.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Monday he believed the 1999 start date for setting up Europe's economic and monetary union EMU was still valid.
"A currency union will be set up according to timetable on January 1, 1999," Asbrink told reporters after visiting some companies in this southern Swedish city.
Asbrink said it was still not clear which countries would be able to participate if the convergence criteria were interpreted strictly.
"We will only see how the criteria are interpreted in spring 1998 when the final decision is taken," Asbrink said.

The row between the Bundesbank and the German government over the revaluation of the central bank's official reserves, the outcome of the French elections and the new government in Britain had made the situation somewhat uncertain.
"We will see what it leads to. The situation is a bit unsure," Asbrink said.

Asked if the Swedish ruling Social Democrats' view on EMU, due to be announced on Tuesday, was affected by the French election, he said, "No, this is an internal process within the Social Democrat party."
Asbrink repeated his view that he was not in support of holding a referendum on EMU.
